ORCH has ruled on the three decisions Step 1 left open. These are routing decisions, not content decisions -- the wording is yours:

RULING 3 -- the status-vocabulary gap is fixed in THIS run, not filed. It blocks Step 5: ISS-0200 cannot be closed without a legal terminal status, and both existing candidates assert something false. Unblock-Everything covers exactly this -- a problem that blocks completion of the current task is fixed here even when it sits outside the original scope. owned_modules is extended to docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md accordingly.

THE THREE EDITS:

(A) docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- "Issue status vocabulary". Add a terminal status for an issue that was investigated, measured, and found to carry no defect. Constraints, all load-bearing: it must NOT weaken what `resolved` asserts (a root cause was actually removed, and a regression test proves it) -- that definition exists because the registry is read as a factual record of what is still broken, and blurring it is the exact harm it guards against. It must demand the SAME evidence discipline as the other two, so it can never become the easy exit for an issue nobody investigated: say what the record must carry to earn it. State that WF-03 and this vocabulary now agree, since WF-03 Step 5 already points at this section as canonical. Name ISS-0200 as the precedent that forced it. Choose the status name yourself.

(B) docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md -- two separate places, and do not merge them:
  (i) Section 2, immediately after the existing "Why this rests on redundancy and not on brevity" block: record the result-side finding as a measured NEGATIVE result. This is the counterpart to ISS-0198's rule and belongs beside it, per ISS-0200's AC3. It MUST be unmistakably labelled as NOT a rule and as stating no threshold -- a later reader must not be able to mistake it for a size constraint on result.summary. Carry the corpus figures, the mechanisms tested and their overlap ceilings, the asymmetry argument (the dispatch defect had a duplicated copy AND an empty structured outlet; neither exists on the result side), and Step 1's own recorded method limitation -- a negative result that hides the weakness of the test that produced it is worth less than no record at all. Its purpose is that the next agent who wonders about result.summary size reads a measurement instead of re-running the investigation.
  (ii) The Enforcement note's existing "Specified but NOT YET RUNNING -- H-SIZE-1/2/3" block: extend H-SIZE-3's emit list with the result.summary figures. H-SIZE-3 is already INFO/never-fails, so this adds no gate. Add NO threshold and NO WARN -- Step 1 was explicit that a WARN here would be a length rule by the back door. The "does not run today" framing already on that block must cover the extension too.

(C) docs/issues/ISS-0191.yaml -- add the same H-SIZE-3 extension to its scope, per ISS-0200's AC5, worded so nothing implies it runs today. Keep it consistent with (B)(ii) -- these two must not drift, which is why both are in this one step.

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 3 -- ISS-0200. All three ORCH-ruled edits made, additive only, 0 deletions across all three files. No result-side size rule was written; the NO-CHANGE verdict was RECORDED as a measured negative result, explicitly labelled as not a rule.

=== (A) docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- new terminal status `no_defect` ===
Chosen name: `no_defect`. Added as a fourth bullet in "Issue status vocabulary", after `instrumented` and before the ISS-0109 worked example, plus a second worked-example paragraph naming ISS-0200 as the precedent that forced it.

`resolved`'s definition is BYTE-IDENTICAL. Its diff, quoted per AC1 -- there is none: `git diff --numstat` on this file reports 52 insertions and 0 deletions, so no line of the `resolved` bullet (lines 187-191, "**a root cause was actually removed**, and a regression test proves it. ... silently misinforms every run that cross-references it.") was touched. The new bullet says so in terms: "Nothing here relaxes `resolved`'s bar by a hair -- that definition stands exactly as written above, and this status exists so that a no-defect outcome stops being tempted to borrow it."

EVIDENCE BAR, written so an uninvestigated issue cannot claim it -- four MUSTs, in the issue file and citing the closing diagnosis handoff by path: (1) the first-hand measurement with producing code/command quoted and real figures, with inherited figures explicitly not counting and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1 applying if the re-measurement disagrees with the filing; (2) the specific candidate mechanisms tested, named individually, INCLUDING the ones the data did not support; (3) the stated limitations of the method, "so a later reader can weigh the negative result instead of inheriting it as settled"; (4) run-id and timestamp. Closed with: "An issue nobody investigated cannot reach `no_defect`: with nothing to quote under (1)-(3) there is nothing to write, and a record that says only 'looked, seemed fine' has not reached a terminal status at all -- it is still `open`." The status is framed as a positive falsifiable claim (checked, measured, not there), not as an absence of findings, so an unbacked `no_defect` misinforms the registry as badly as a false `resolved`.

WF-03 AGREEMENT stated explicitly in its own paragraph: WF-03 Step 1 has always licensed a reasoned NO-CHANGE verdict and WF-03 Step 5 already points at this section as canonical, but the list offered no legal terminal value -- `resolved` would assert a removal that never happened, `instrumented` shipped work that does not exist.

=== (B)(i) HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 -- the measured negative result ===
Inserted immediately after the "Why this rests on redundancy and not on brevity" block ends ("...it is not a budget any dispatch must meet.") and immediately before "**Legal `result.status` values**". It opens: "**A MEASURED NEGATIVE RESULT -- NOT A RULE, AND IT STATES NO THRESHOLD.**" and states in the same paragraph that nothing in it constrains the length of any result.summary, that no target or budget is stated or to be inferred, and that it must not be cited as a size rule.

Carries the corpus figures: 605 parseable / 0 unparseable / 60 runs; len(result.summary) median 2,986, p90 8,493, p95 12,323, max 47,036, total 2,599,136; len(task.description) median 704, p90 3,940, p95 5,737, max 19,040, total 889,118; pooled 2.92x; per-handoff ratio (n=601) median 3.53x, p90 13.86x, max 43.5x. The six mechanisms tested are each named with n, median and max, with the note that none of the 120 large summaries exceeded 0.30 on any axis and that the dispatch-side structural screen fired 20/20 there but only 46/120 here and did not select. Step 1's METHOD LIMITATION appears in its own labelled bullet: the 8-gram test detects verbatim restatement and is under-powered against paraphrase; calibrated against the 26 large dispatches it returns median 0.054 / p90 0.200 / max 0.347, so the figures are load-bearing only comparatively, with evidence density (median 65.3% of segments carrying a digit, path or identifier; minimum 36.7%) and the hand-read of the least-evidence-dense large summary named as the independent support. The ASYMMETRY ARGUMENT closes it: the dispatch defect had a duplicated copy AND an empty structured outlet (requirement_text == {} in 66 of 69); neither exists here (artifacts_out non-empty on 449 of 605); a duplicated copy drifts from its source, whereas an attestation IS the source and section 4 makes the acting agent the only party who can write it. Ends: "no result-side entry in the inline-vs-artifacts_in table, no required shape, no length target."
The purpose sentence is in the opening paragraph verbatim -- recorded "so the next agent who wonders whether the rule above should have a result-side counterpart reads the answer instead of re-running the investigation."

issues.description: Naming decision recorded for the REVIEWER gate rather than left implicit: the new terminal status is `no_defect`. Alternatives considered and rejected -- `no_change` (describes the RUN's action rather than the ISSUE's truth, and would read as 'we chose not to act', which is exactly the weaker claim the evidence bar exists to prevent) and `not_reproduced` (asserts only that one attempt failed to reproduce, a weaker and different claim than 'measured, no root cause present'). `no_defect` states a finding about the registry's subject matter, which is what the registry is read for.

For Step 5's awareness, not a defect in this step: ISS-0200 will be the FIRST record to carry `status: no_defect`, and the new vocabulary bullet requires four items in the issue file itself -- the measurement with producing code quoted, the mechanisms tested including the unsupported ones, the method limitations, and the run-id and timestamp. Step 5 must write all four into docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml citing handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json by path. A first use that does not meet its own new bar would be the worst possible precedent for it.
